citations.title: Employee Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: (a) The facility designates a manager in writing. The manager must be on duty 40 hrs/week and may manage only one facility, except a small Type A manager may oversee up to 4 facilities with no more than 16 residents in total. A backup is named in writing. Large-facility managers need an associate's degree, a bachelor's degree, or a high school credential plus 1 year of management experience. The manager completes a 24-hr ALF management course by the first anniversary, including 8 hrs on the standards within 3 months, plus 12 hrs of CE a year. (b) An attendant is in the facility whenever residents are present. (c) Staffing policies set ratios from residents' service plans. The normal 24-hr staffing pattern is disclosed before admission and posted monthly. Night staff: small Type A immediately available; large Type A and all Type B immediately available and awake. (d) 4-hr orientation for all staff. 16 hrs of attendant on-the-job training in the first 16 hrs after orientation. 6 hrs/yr of direct-care education, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management. Annual geriatric in-service for nurses, CNAs and medication aides.

citations.title: Training Requirements for Staff Providing Personal Care Services to a Resident With Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder in a Facility that is Not an Alzheimer's Certified Facility
citations.requirement: Manager: 4 hrs of training plus a competency evaluation, then 2 hrs of annual CE. Personal care staff: 4 hrs plus a competency evaluation before performing personal care, then 2 hrs of CE. Non-direct staff with recurring contact (housekeeping, front desk, maintenance) complete training and a competency evaluation on Alzheimer's disease, person-centered care and behaviors. Certificates are issued to staff and kept per records retention policy. Training carries over if the employment gap is under 2 years.

citations.title: All Staff Policy for Residents with Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder
citations.requirement: Requires a facility policy on all staff and residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders. Section number and title verified from the Subchapter E table of contents, and §553.254(a)(2) confirms the §553.254 training may satisfy it. The full text was not retrieved, so confirm the policy's required content against the rule before finalizing.

citations.title: Human Resources
citations.requirement: Personnel files hold: criminal history check documentation; annual Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) and Nurse Aide Registry (NAR) checks; TB screening; vaccine-policy compliance or exemption; the signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report; and a signed disclosure statement on §250.006 convictions and residence in another state in the past 5 years. Before hire, search the EMR and NAR. Do not hire or keep anyone listed as unemployable or convicted of a barring offense. Repeat searches at least every 12 months. A name-based criminal check is required in each prior state of residence in the past 5 years; the person may be hired pending results but not in a direct-contact position. Suspend, and do not reinstate, an employee HHSC finds engaged in reportable conduct until appeals are exhausted. Reportable conduct includes abuse or neglect causing harm, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, and emotional or verbal abuse causing harm.

citations.title: Admission Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: (a) Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs cannot be met. Use a written admission agreement. Give the disclosure statement and rate schedule. Provide the Memory Care Disclosure Statement if memory care is marketed (plus HHSC Form 3641 if Alzheimer's certified). Physician exam within 30 days before or 14 days after admission. Collect the listed identifying information. (b) Comprehensive assessment and service plan within 14 days of admission. Update the plan annually and on significant change. (c) Give the disclosure statement before admission and the Resident's Bill of Rights. Give and document family receipt of the HHSC abuse hotline number. Keep written resident policies and give notice of changes before they take effect. Give the restraint/seclusion notice and the emergency plan or evacuation summary. (d) Advance directive policy and notice. $500 penalty for failure to inform. (e) Inappropriate placement: Forms 1124, 1125, 1126 within 10 working days; evacuation waiver; discharge within 30 days if the facility will not retain.

citations.title: Coordination of Care
citations.requirement: (a) Medication administration, supervision, self-administration, storage and disposal. (b) Accident, injury and acute illness response and documentation; first aid supplies. (c) Health care professionals and outside HCSSA services; no ongoing nursing-facility-level services. (d) Activity program at least weekly. (e) Dietary services. (f) Infection prevention and control, TB screening and the vaccine policy. (g) Restraints and seclusion (the heading was verified, but the subsection text was cut off in the retrieved copy; review it before finalizing).

citations.title: Health maintenance activities
citations.requirement: Personal care staff may perform a health maintenance activity (HMA) without delegation only when an RN has assessed and documented that it qualifies. The resident or representative must direct the task and agree in writing, and the condition must be stable and predictable. The RN reassesses on any change of condition, at least annually, and at least every 6 months for residents with Alzheimer's or in a certified facility or unit. Activities that are not HMAs require RN delegation under 22 TAC Chapter 225 and §553.261(a)(1)(A)(iii).

citations.title: Resident Records and Retention
citations.requirement: Records are confidential and safeguarded. A record contains the admission form, assessments, service plan, physician orders, advance directives, the physician exam, professional service documentation, and guardianship papers. Records are available to residents, legal representatives and HHSC. Keep a simple financial record of charges and of any personal funds handled. Issue receipts on request. Request the guardianship court order and letters at admission and at each annual assessment, make a follow-up request within 30 days, and keep the results.

citations.title: Rights
citations.requirement: (a) Give each resident the Residents' Bill of Rights and post it in each resident's primary language. The rights include freedom from abuse and from restraint used for discipline or convenience, restraint only on written physician authorization or in an emergency, and complaint without reprisal. They also include unopened mail, visitors at any reasonable hour, managing one's own finances with at least quarterly accounting, record access, choice of physician, participation in the service plan, refusal of treatment, a locked personal area, notice by day 30 of Medicare/Medicaid entitlement, discharge only on listed grounds with 30 days' written notice, and ombudsman access. (b) Post the Providers' Bill of Rights. A provider may terminate for just cause on 30 days' written notice, or immediately for a serious threat after notice to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858. (c) Allow HHSC access. (d) Authorized electronic monitoring (AEM).

citations.title: Access to Residents and Records by the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
citations.requirement: The State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns get immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility and to residents during business or visiting hours. The State Ombudsman and certified ombudsmen also get access at other times if circumstances require. They get access to resident records with consent or as the rule otherwise allows. HIPAA does not bar release to the ombudsman, who is a health oversight agency.

citations.title: Postings
citations.requirement: Post in a public area: the license; the HHSC complaint-procedure sign; the notice that inspection reports are available and the HHSC toll-free number; the most recent inspection report; the Residents' Bill of Rights; the Providers' Bill of Rights; the local ombudsman number and the 1-800-252-2412 toll-free number; the normal 24-hr staffing pattern; and the sign 'Cases of Suspected Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation must be reported to HHSC by calling 1-800-458-9858.'

citations.title: Advertisements, Solicitations, and Promotional Material
citations.requirement: Rules on advertising and promotional material. Section number and title verified from the Subchapter E table of contents. The text was not retrieved, so draft the policy after reading the rule. Note §553.259(a)(4) on memory care marketing.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation Reportable to HHSC by Facilities
citations.requirement: Staff with cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed by abuse, neglect or exploitation, or died from abuse or neglect, report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 (or the HHSC website) and to municipal police or the county sheriff. The report includes the resident's name, age and address, the responsible person, the nature of the condition, the basis of knowledge, and other relevant information. The facility makes an immediate oral report, investigates, and sends a written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report. No retaliation. Staff sign a statement, as a condition of employment, that they may be criminally liable for failure to report. The facility follows its internal prevention, detection and reporting policies.

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response
citations.requirement: Document a risk assessment (fire, outage, flood, hurricane or severe weather, epidemic, cyber attack, etc.). Keep a written plan covering the 8 core functions: direction and control, warning, communication, sheltering, evacuation, transportation, health and medical needs, and resource management. Coordinate with the local Emergency Management Coordinator. Designate an Emergency Preparedness Coordinator and an alternate. Review and update the plan annually and within 30 days after an event, drill shortcoming or rule change. Give residents and representatives the plan or an evacuation summary at admission. Register with 2-1-1 Texas and tell residents how to register for evacuation assistance. Shelter-in-place temperatures must be 68–82°F. Notify the HHSC regional office and the EMC on a decision to shelter or evacuate. Keep written acknowledgments with a receiving facility and an alternate. Plan for pets and service animals. Only subsections (a)–(i)(2)(D)(i) were retrieved; review the remaining subsections (staff accompaniment, training, drills, return) before finalizing.

citations.title: Types of Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Type A: residents can evacuate without staff help, with no routine night attendance. Type B: residents may need evacuation help and night attendance but may not be permanently bedfast.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Small facility: licensed for 16 or fewer residents. Large facility: 17 or more. Defines terms used in the staffing, HMA, infection control and AEM rules.

citations.title: Licensing criteria, general application requirements, time periods, initial license procedures
citations.requirement: Initial application through the HHSC portal (TULIP) with the local fire authority documentation and the pre-licensure training certificate. A Life Safety Code inspection and a health inspection are required. After the LSC inspection, 1–3 residents may be admitted. HHSC must deny an applicant whose health care or long-term care license was revoked within the last 5 years or who is excluded from Medicare/Medicaid (§553.17). Applications still incomplete 120 days after receipt are denied (§553.21).

citations.title: License Fees
citations.requirement: 3-year license fee of $300 + $15 per bed, capped at $2,250. Alzheimer's certification +$300. $15 per bed for a capacity increase. Late-renewal fee of half the basic fee if filed later than 45 days before expiration. Possible trust fund assessment (§553.47(d)). Expedited LSC inspection fee (§553.47(g)).

citations.title: Facility Construction; Fire Protection Systems for New Small Type A / Type B Facilities
citations.requirement: Construction and life safety standards in separate divisions for existing and new facilities, small and large, Type A and Type B. New small Type A and Type B facilities need an NFPA 13, 13R or 13D sprinkler system with electrical supervision, and a manual fire alarm with smoke detection (§§553.215, 553.225). Residents' evacuation capability must match the NFPA 101 and Subchapter D requirements (§553.259(a)(1)).

citations.title: Additional Licensing Standards for Certified Alzheimer's Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Added staffing, training, admission, disclosure (Form 3641) and physical plant standards (§553.311) for an Alzheimer's certified facility or unit. Certification applies to Type B only (§553.27).

citations.title: Inspections, Investigations, and Informal Dispute Resolution
citations.requirement: HHSC inspections and complaint investigations, and the informal dispute resolution process. Section range verified from the Chapter 553 table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: Enforcement remedies, including administrative penalties, license actions and plans of correction. Subchapter verified from the Chapter 553 table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Nurse Aide Registry and Criminal History Checks for Facility Employees
citations.requirement: Verify employability through criminal history and registry checks, with an annual registry search. §250.006 lists the convictions that bar employment (referenced in §553.257).

citations.title: Assisted Living Facility Licensing Act
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for ALF licensure by HHSC, including plan review (§247.0261, per HHSC guidance).

citations.title: STAR+PLUS Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Program
citations.requirement: STAR+PLUS HCBS eligibility and interest-list rules for members who may receive assisted living services.

citations.title: STAR+PLUS Handbook – Assisted Living Services
citations.requirement: Housing options (apartment vs non-apartment) are stated in the MCO contract. Members live in an ALF contracted with their MCO. Health assessment and emergency training within 3 days of admission. At least 4 social activities a week. Next-business-day reporting of changes to the MCO. Member trust fund records. Room and board cannot be waived (a lower amount may be accepted), is prorated in the first month, and is due on a written date.

citations.title: Medication services in assisted living facilities
citations.requirement: HHSC guidance on medication administration, supervision and self-administration. Only a licensed nurse, a permitted medication aide under a nurse on duty or on call, or an RN-delegated employee may administer medications. A medication aide permit takes 100 classroom + 20 lab + 10 clinical hours and an exam, with annual renewal.

citations.title: State responsibilities – screening and enrollment of managed care network providers
citations.requirement: Managed care network providers, including STAR+PLUS ALFs, must be screened and enrolled with the State.

citations.title: Alzheimer's certification of a Type B facility or unit; license renewal; capacity change
citations.requirement: Only a Type B facility or unit may be Alzheimer's certified (§553.27). Renew the license on time (§553.33). Get HHSC approval before adding beds (§553.39). Sections are present in the research section list; text not re-fetched.

citations.title: Community Homes for Disabled Persons Location Act
citations.requirement: An ALF licensed under HSC Ch. 247 can qualify as a community home. Up to 6 persons with disabilities + 2 supervisors. No community home within one-half mile of another.

citations.title: Ombudsman access to facilities, residents and records
citations.requirement: Federal basis for the ombudsman's access rights, as incorporated in 26 TAC §553.269(b)–(c).

policies.title: License Type, Capacity, Renewal and Regulatory Compliance
federal: Title VI, Civil Rights Act (45 CFR Part 80)
state_specifics: Type A: residents evacuate without staff help, no routine night attendance. Type B: may need evacuation help and night attendance, not permanently bedfast (§553.5).
Small = 16 or fewer residents; large = 17 or more (§553.3).
3-year license fee: $300 + $15/bed, cap $2,250. Alzheimer's certification +$300. Capacity increase $15/bed, with HHSC approval first (§§553.47, 553.39).
File renewal at least 45 days before expiration or pay a late fee of half the basic fee (§§553.33, 553.47).
Staff cooperate with HHSC inspections, complaint investigations, informal dispute resolution and enforcement (Subchapters G and H).

policies.title: Policy and Procedure Manual Submission for Licensure (Including Alzheimer's Certification)
state_specifics: A good-standing applicant requesting a license before the health inspection submits this manual through the HHSC online portal (TULIP) with evidence of §553.257(b) compliance and staff credentials under §553.253.
An applicant requesting Alzheimer's certification before the health inspection also submits the Subchapter F policies for approval, with documentation of Subchapter F and §553.257(b) compliance.
Certification applies to a Type B facility or unit only (§553.27). Use Form 3721 with Form 3720.
The application packet needs the local fire authority documentation and the pre-licensure training certificate.
The Administrator keeps a credential and compliance file for each employee, ready for submission.

policies.title: Fire Safety Plan, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: The written fire safety plan is in effect at all times. Supervisory personnel get copies, and a copy is kept readily available in the facility.
The plan covers evacuation to an area of refuge, evacuation from the building when necessary, and special staff actions and fire protection procedures to keep each resident safe.
Large Type B: include the NFPA 101 'Procedure in Case of Fire' provisions (§19.7.2 existing / §18.7.2 new).
Review the plan at least annually and revise it. Instruct employees on their duties at least annually and whenever the plan is revised.
Keep the plan current with residents' evacuation capabilities, consistent with Type A/B status.

policies.title: Smoking, E-Cigarette/Vaping and Oxygen Safety
federal: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000 series (employee exposure, as applicable)
state_specifics: The written smoking policy must be enforced even if the policy is that smoking is not permitted. It must address e-cigarettes and vaping devices.
If smoking is permitted: designated smoking areas for residents and staff, and noncombustible, safely designed ashtrays.
Written procedures for resident use, storage and handling of oxygen cylinders and liquid oxygen containers in residents' possession and control.
Staff review oxygen and smoking rules at orientation and annually.

policies.title: Fire Alarm and Fire Sprinkler Inspection, Testing and Maintenance
state_specifics: Fire alarm: inspect, test and maintain per NFPA 72 (NFPA 720 where CO detection is provided) at least every six months, through a contract with a State Fire Marshal-registered company.
Sprinkler system (if equipped): inspect, test and maintain per NFPA 25 at least every six months.
Keep documentation onsite.
New small Type A and Type B facilities must have an NFPA 13, 13R or 13D sprinkler system with electrical supervision and a manual fire alarm with smoke detection (§§553.215, 553.225).

policies.title: Manager Designation, Qualifications and Backup
state_specifics: Designate the manager in writing with authority over operation. The manager is on duty 40 hrs/week and may manage only one facility (a small Type A manager may oversee up to 4 facilities with no more than 16 residents total).

Small facility: high school diploma or equivalent. Large facility: associate's degree (nursing, health care management or related), bachelor's degree, or high school credential + 1 year of management experience.
Manager completes the 24-hr ALF management course by the first anniversary, with 8 hrs on the standards within 3 months, and 12 hrs of CE every year.
Designate in writing an employee competent and authorized to act in the manager's absence.

policies.title: Staffing Levels, 24-Hour Staffing Pattern and Night Staffing
state_specifics: There is no numeric ratio. Staffing ratios are set from residents' needs identified in service plans, and an attendant is in the facility whenever residents are present.
Disclose the normal 24-hr staffing pattern to prospective residents and post it monthly.
Staff must be sufficient for order, safety and cleanliness, medication help, meals, laundry, supervision and safe evacuation.
Night shift: small Type A, immediately available. Large Type A and all Type B, immediately available and awake.

policies.title: Orientation, Attendant On-the-Job Training and Annual In-Service Training
state_specifics: All staff: 4-hr orientation before assuming job duties. It covers abuse/neglect reporting, confidentiality, universal precautions, when to notify the manager, residents' rights, and emergency/evacuation procedures.

Attendants: 16 hrs supervised on-the-job training within the first 16 hrs after orientation. It covers ADLs, health conditions, accident prevention, first aid, disruptive behavior, behavior management and fall prevention.
Direct care staff: 6 hrs/year, competency-based, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management.
Licensed nurses, CNAs and certified medication aides: annual in-service suited to their job duties.
Medication aide permit: 100 classroom + 20 lab + 10 clinical hrs, annual renewal.

policies.category: §553.254 / §553.255 Alzheimer's Staff Training and All-Staff Policy
policies.title: Dementia Training and All-Staff Policy for Residents with Alzheimer's Disease or Related Disorders
state_specifics: Manager: 4 hrs + competency evaluation, then 2 hrs annual CE. Personal care staff: 4 hrs + competency evaluation before personal care, then 2 hrs CE.
Non-direct staff with recurring contact (housekeeping, front desk, maintenance) complete training and a competency evaluation.
Written policy requires direct-care staff to complete dementia training and ensures care meets each resident's diagnosis-specific needs.
Training content: symptoms of dementia, stages of Alzheimer's, person-centered behavioral interventions, and communication.
Issue certificates and keep them per retention policy. Training carries over if the employment gap is under 2 years.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file holds: criminal history check, annual EMR check, annual NAR check, initial TB screening, vaccine-policy compliance or exemption, signed criminal liability statement, and signed §250.006 disclosure statement (including residence in another state in the past 5 years).
Files are current and complete, and training certificates are filed.
Keep files confidential and available to HHSC.

policies.title: Background Checks, Employee Registries and Staff Conduct
federal: Fair Credit Reporting Act (if using consumer reporting agencies)
42 CFR 1001 (OIG exclusion screening for Medicaid providers)
state_specifics: Before hire, search the Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) and Nurse Aide Registry (NAR), and repeat at least every 12 months. File the results.
Do not hire or keep anyone listed as unemployable or barred by HSC §250.006.
Name-based criminal check in each state of residence in the past 5 years. The person may be hired pending results but not in a direct-contact position.
Suspend, and do not reinstate, an employee HHSC finds engaged in reportable conduct until appeals are exhausted.
Give EMR notification per §561.3. Staff conduct and professional boundaries rules apply to all staff.

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Admission Criteria and Admission Health Examination
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs the facility cannot meet and who cannot get the services from an outside resource. Additional services need written concurrence of the resident, physician or legal representative.
Check that the resident's evacuation capability matches the license type (§553.259(a)(1)).
Physician health exam within 30 days before or 14 days after admission.

At admission, collect identifying information: name, SSN, usual residence, sex, marital status, DOB, place of birth, occupation, emergency contacts, physician, pharmacy preference, and Medicaid/Medicare number.

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Disclosure Statement, Rates, Fees and Refunds
state_specifics: Written admission agreement stating services and charges, with a statement if services or supplies could be a Medicare benefit.
Share the disclosure statement, rate schedule and service plan with outside resources providing additional services.
Memory Care Disclosure Statement (Form 3650) if the facility advertises memory care. State whether it is Alzheimer's certified (Form 3641 if certified).
Agreement states deposit, refund and discharge terms.

policies.title: Resident Assessment, Reassessment and Individual Service Plan
state_specifics: Comprehensive assessment (items A–T) and service plan within 14 days of admission.
Service plan signed by the resident or responsible person. Update annually and on significant change.
Respite and emergency admission provisions apply.
STAR+PLUS members also get a health assessment within 3 days of admission (see MED-01).

policies.title: Admission Packet, Written Resident Policies and Required Notices
state_specifics: Before admission, explain and give the disclosure statement (document receipt), the Residents' Bill of Rights, and the HHSC abuse/neglect/exploitation hotline number to the resident and family (document receipt).
Written resident policies cover residents accepted, services, charges, refunds, responsibilities, privileges and rules.
Give policies to residents or representatives at admission, with documented notice of changes before they take effect.
Give HHSC rules and facility policy on restraint and seclusion before or at admission.
Give a written copy of the emergency plan or an evacuation summary.

policies.title: Advance Directives
state_specifics: Written policy on implementing advance directives, with a clear statement of any procedure the facility is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold.
Give written notice to residents at admission, including the order of preference for incapacitated residents.
Failure to inform carries a $500 penalty (§553.259(d)).

policies.title: Aging in Place, Inappropriate Placement, Evacuation Waiver, Discharge and Transfer
state_specifics: Inappropriate placement procedure: Forms 1124, 1125 and 1126, plus a detailed emergency plan, within 10 working days.
The disclosure statement describes the waiver process and the aging-in-place policy.
If the waiver is not obtained, discharge within 30 days.
Discharge only on grounds listed in the Bill of Rights, with 30 days' written notice. A serious threat allows immediate termination after notice to HHSC at 800-458-9858 (§553.267(b)).

policies.title: Medication Administration, Supervision and Self-Administration
federal: Controlled Substances Act (21 CFR 1300 series, as applicable)
state_specifics: Administer per physician's orders. Only a licensed nurse, a permitted medication aide under a nurse on duty or on call, or an RN-delegated employee may administer (PL 2023-22).
Keep a medication profile record per resident with name, strength, dosage, amount received, directions, route, Rx number, pharmacy and date issued.
Staff supervision is limited to the listed tasks. Monthly counseling for self-administering residents.
Report unusual reactions immediately. Keep a written record of missed doses.

policies.title: Medication Storage, Controlled Drug Diversion Prevention and Disposal
federal: DEA 21 CFR 1317 (disposal of controlled substances, as applicable)
state_specifics: Lock all medications. Store each resident's medication separately, refrigerated items in a locked refrigerator, and poisons and 'external use only' items separately.
If controlled drugs are stored, the policy must address diversion prevention.
Discontinued, deceased-resident and expired medications are kept separate and disposed of by a Texas-registered pharmacist.
Needles and syringes per 25 TAC §§1.131–1.137. Release medications to discharged residents on signed receipt.

policies.title: Accident, Injury, Acute Illness, Change of Condition, Falls and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Arrange emergency care or transfer. Immediately notify the physician and next of kin, responsible party or placing agency.
Describe and document each event on a separate report with final disposition.
Keep first aid supplies for burns, cuts and poisoning in one location.
Falls prevention (1 hr annual staff training) and skin integrity are addressed in service plans and in the change-of-condition notification process.

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Provide an activity or social program for residents at least weekly.
STAR+PLUS members: at least 4 social activities per week.
Individualize activities to resident interests and abilities. Memory care units have additional standards (CAL-02).

policies.title: Food Service, Dietary Services and Therapeutic Diets
federal: FDA Food Code (as adopted by Texas, for food safety)
state_specifics: Designate a person responsible for food service. Serve at least three meals daily with no more than a 16-hr span between evening meal and breakfast.
Plan menus one week ahead, follow them, document variations, and keep records 30 days.
Therapeutic diets per physician order (dietitian-calculated where required).
Keep a four-day supply of staples and a one-day supply of perishables.
Follow items (1)–(18) on food sources, storage, temperatures, handwashing, sanitation and employee illness.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control Program
state_specifics: Establish, implement, enforce and maintain a policy for a safe, sanitary environment that prevents the spread of disease.

Written procedures for: monitoring key infectious agents including multidrug-resistant organisms; PPE and hand hygiene; cleaning and disinfecting surfaces; universal precautions; and removing soiled items from the environment at least daily.
Written procedure for making a rapid influenza diagnostic test available to a resident with flu-like symptoms.

policies.title: Communicable Disease, Tuberculosis Screening and Vaccine-Preventable Disease Policy
state_specifics: Report residents with reportable diseases to the local health authority.
Employee TB screening within 2 weeks of employment and annually. Resident TB screening consistent with CDC guidelines.
Exclude infected employees from food handling or direct care.
Vaccine policy (HSC Ch. 224) must: specify vaccines by risk, verify, handle exemptions, protect residents from exempt staff, bar retaliation, keep records and set discipline.
The policy may include conscience exemptions and restrict contact during a public health disaster.

policies.title: Restraints, Seclusion and Wheelchair Self-Release Seat Belts
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F) (HCBS modifications of rights, Medicaid residents)
state_specifics: Restraints for behavioral management, convenience or discipline and all seclusion are prohibited.
Restraint only on written physician authorization (circumstances and duration) or in a behavioral emergency.
Follow the rules on prohibited restraint types, the acceptable hold, post-restraint physician appointment, 24-hr notification and no retaliation for reporting.
Allow wheelchair self-release seat belts when the four conditions are met. Restraint-free facilities give residents a written statement.

policies.title: Nursing Services, Delegation, Health Maintenance Activities and Outside Health Professionals (Home Health/Hospice)
state_specifics: Coordinate services within each professional's scope. Do not provide ongoing services comparable to a nursing facility. Residents may contract with a HCSSA or independent professional.
Personal care staff perform a health maintenance activity (HMA) without delegation only after RN assessment and documentation under 22 TAC §225.6.
Conditions: stable and predictable, the resident directs the task, and written agreement.
RN reassessment on change of condition, at least annually, and every 6 months for residents with Alzheimer's. Non-HMA tasks need RN delegation under 22 TAC Ch. 225.

policies.title: Resident Records, Financial Records, Retention and Guardianship Documentation
state_specifics: Records are confidential and safeguarded against unauthorized use, loss or destruction.
Contents: admission form, assessments, service plan, physician orders, advance directives, physician exam, professional service documentation and guardianship papers.
Records are available to residents, legal representatives and HHSC.
Keep a simple financial record of charges and any personal funds handled, and issue receipts on request.
Request the guardianship order and letters at admission, on appointment and at each annual assessment. Follow up within 30 days and keep copies.

policies.title: Death of a Resident and Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Report a death resulting from abuse or neglect to HHSC at 800-458-9858 and to law enforcement (§553.273).
Notify the physician, next of kin or responsible party, and any hospice or HCSSA provider.
Release the resident's property and records per the admission agreement and policy.
Self-report fires and disaster-related deaths or injuries per §553.275(o) (see EMG-08).
STAR+PLUS: report changes in condition to the MCO by the next business day.

policies.title: Residents' Bill of Rights and Providers' Bill of Rights
state_specifics: Give each resident the Bill of Rights and post it in each resident's primary language.

Rights include freedom from abuse and from restraint, complaint without reprisal, unopened mail, visitors at reasonable hours, managing one's own finances with at least quarterly accounting, record access, physician choice, refusal of treatment and a locked personal area.
Notify residents by day 30 of Medicare/Medicaid entitlement.
Discharge only on listed grounds with 30 days' written notice. Post the Providers' Bill of Rights.
Allow HHSC and local authority access to residents.

policies.title: Authorized Electronic Monitoring (AEM)
state_specifics: Permit AEM. Never refuse admission or discharge a resident because of an AEM request.
Forms: Form 3100 on admission, Form 0066 request, Form 0067 roommate consent.
Post a notice at the room entrance and an 8.5 x 11 'Electronic Monitoring' notice at the main entrance.
Make reasonable physical accommodation. Report abuse or neglect seen in recordings.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Residents may complain without reprisal.
Post the HHSC complaint-procedure sign and the toll-free ombudsman number 800-252-2412.
Document each complaint, the investigation and the response, and review them in QAPI.
Any abuse, neglect or exploitation complaint goes through ABU-01.

policies.title: Resident Funds, Personal Property and Trust Accounts
state_specifics: Residents manage their own finances, with at least a quarterly accounting for any funds the facility handles.
Keep a record of charges and any personal funds entrusted, and issue receipts on request.
STAR+PLUS: keep member trust fund records. Room and board cannot be waived (a lower amount may be accepted), is prorated in month one and is due on a written date.
Financial exploitation of $25 or more is reportable conduct.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality, HIPAA, Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI, Civil Rights Act (45 CFR Part 80)
state_specifics: Resident information is confidential. Release only with consent or as allowed by law.
HIPAA does not bar release to the ombudsman, who is a health oversight agency.
The Residents' Bill of Rights is posted in each resident's primary language.
No discrimination in admission or services on a protected basis. Provide interpreters and auxiliary aids as needed.

policies.title: State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Access to Residents and Records
state_specifics: The State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns get immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility and residents during business or visiting hours.
The State Ombudsman and certified ombudsmen also get access at other times if circumstances require.
Access to records is with consent or as the rule otherwise allows.
State Ombudsman toll-free number: 800-252-2412.

policies.title: Required Postings, Advertising and Promotional Material
state_specifics: Post in a public area: the license, the HHSC complaint-procedure sign, the inspection-report notice and most recent inspection report, and both Bills of Rights.
Post local and State Ombudsman numbers (800-252-2412) and the normal 24-hr staffing pattern (updated monthly).
Post the sign: 'Cases of Suspected Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation must be reported to HHSC by calling 1-800-458-9858.'
Advertising must comply with §553.272, including the memory care marketing rule in §553.259(a)(4).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention, Detection and Reporting
state_specifics: Any staff member with cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed, or died from abuse or neglect, reports to HHSC at 800-458-9858 (or the HHSC website) and to local police or the county sheriff.
The report includes the resident's name, age and address, the responsible person, the nature and extent of the condition, the basis of knowledge, and other relevant information.
Follow internal prevention, detection and reporting procedures (§553.273(b)).
Reportable conduct includes abuse or neglect causing harm, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, and emotional or verbal abuse causing harm.

policies.title: Abuse Investigation, Written Report, Non-Retaliation and Staff Acknowledgment
state_specifics: Make an immediate oral report to HHSC, investigate, and send a written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report.
No retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith.
As a condition of employment, every staff member signs a statement of possible criminal liability for failure to report. File it in the personnel record.
Protect the resident during the investigation and suspend implicated staff as required by §553.257.

policies.title: Incident Reporting, Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Self-report reportable incidents through TULIP or Complaint and Incident Intake at 800-458-9858.
Document accidents and injuries on a separate report (§553.261(b)).
Elopement procedure: immediate search, 911 and law enforcement, then notification of the physician and the responsible party.
Review each incident in QAPI and update service plans.

policies.title: Emergency Risk Assessment and Written Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan
state_specifics: Document a risk assessment for fire/explosion, power/telecom/water outage, wildfire, hazardous materials, active shooter/bomb threat, flood, hurricane/severe weather, epidemic/pandemic, cyber-attack and loss of all or part of the facility.
The written plan addresses the 8 core functions: direction and control, warning, communication, sheltering, evacuation, transportation, health and medical needs, and resource management.
The plan documents Emergency Management Coordinator (EMC) contact information and how to communicate with the EMC.
The plan names where the current resident list is kept, identifying residents with Alzheimer's/related disorders, evacuation waivers, and mobility or special needs.
Notify the EMC of the plan.

policies.title: Emergency Plan Maintenance, Staff and Resident Training, and Drills
state_specifics: Keep a printed copy in a central location accessible to staff, residents and representatives.
Review at least annually and after events. Update within 30 days of drill shortcomings or policy/rule changes. Document reviews.
Give residents or representatives the plan or an evacuation summary. Tell residents how to register with 2-1-1 Texas, and register the facility as a provider.
Annual staff training, and training on responsibilities before assuming duties and when they change.
At least one unannounced drill per year. Offer and document training for residents, representatives and emergency contacts.

policies.title: Emergency Direction and Control, Warning and Communication
state_specifics: Designate an Emergency Preparedness Coordinator (EPC) and an alternate. Assign duties by function or position.
Warning: how the EPC is notified (including off hours, weekends and holidays), how people in the facility are kept informed, and monitoring of local news and weather.
Communication: primary and alternate modes, when to call 911, and where the contact lists are kept.
Notify staff, residents, representatives, emergency contacts, HCSSAs, receiving facilities, drivers and the EMC.

policies.title: Sheltering in Place
state_specifics: Decision procedure for remaining in the facility. It requires access to medication, records, equipment, water and food (including special diets), and sheltering staff.
Safe power, with temperatures kept between 68 and 82°F.
After deciding to remain, notify the HHSC regional office and the EMC.

policies.title: Evacuation and Emergency Transportation
state_specifics: Evacuation destinations and routes with a map. Decision procedure with contingencies and a plan for pets and service animals.
Written acknowledgment from at least one receiving facility or destination and one alternate.
Procedures for notifying HHSC and the EMC, staff accompaniment, resident accounting and tracking, release of resident information, re-entry determination and return of residents.
Transportation: arrange enough vehicles, designate drivers, and transport residents and staff safely with oxygen, medications, records, food, water and equipment.

policies.title: Emergency Health and Medical Needs and Resource Management
federal: HIPAA 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7) (contingency plan principles for records)
state_specifics: Identify residents' special services (dialysis, oxygen, hospice) and how they continue. Notify HCSSAs and independent professionals of an evacuation.
Plan for obtaining, transporting and storing medications, records, food, water, equipment and supplies.
Keep medications secure and at proper temperature.
Safeguard confidentiality, security and integrity of resident records.

policies.title: Receiving Facility Procedures (Only If the Facility Will Accept Evacuees)
state_specifics: Include this policy only if the facility will act as a receiving facility for another ALF.
Procedures follow conditions (1)–(5): capacity limits, safety, ability to meet needs, log, and continuity-of-care items.
Keep a written acknowledgment with each sending facility.

policies.title: Disaster Incident Self-Reports and Emergency Response System
state_specifics: Fire: call 800-458-9858 and submit Form 3707 within 15 days.
Death, serious injury or threat from a disaster: call immediately and submit Provider Investigation Report Form 3613-A within 5 working days.
The administrator and a designee enroll in the HHSC Emergency Response System and respond in HHSC's format.

policies.title: Certified Alzheimer's Facility: Manager Qualifications and Staff Training
state_specifics: Applies only to a Type B facility or unit that is certified or advertises specialized dementia care.
Manager/unit supervisor: age 21 plus education/experience options and 6 hrs annual dementia continuing education (§553.301).
Staff: 4-hr dementia-specific orientation. Attendants: 16 hrs on-the-job training plus 12 hrs annual Alzheimer's in-service (§553.303).
Training covers ADLs, dementia-specific emergency/evacuation procedures, dysfunctional behavior and behavior management.

policies.title: Certified Alzheimer's Facility: Staffing and Activities Program
state_specifics: Sufficient staff for residents' needs. In facilities or units with 17 or more residents, two staff are immediately available whenever residents are present (§553.305).
Planned, structured, individualized program mixing cognitive, recreational and ADL activities, with daily offerings and a monthly schedule (§553.309).
Activity director for 20 hrs weekly in facilities of 17 or more residents. The responsible employee gets 6 hrs annual CE.

policies.title: Certified Alzheimer's Facility: Admission, Assessment and Service Plan
state_specifics: Use Form 3641. Give it to any inquirer.
Pre-admission procedures (application, interviews, home visits) ensure appropriate placement.
Comprehensive assessment and individualized service plan within 14 days and annually. Update the plan on significant change.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The governing body (the licensee on the HHSC application) is accountable for compliance with HSC Ch. 247 and 26 TAC Ch. 553.
It appoints the manager in writing (§553.253).
Report ownership and manager changes to HHSC on Form 3720.
Review this manual at least annually and whenever the rules change (watch proposed Rule 25R031).

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Track incidents, falls, medication errors, complaints, drill results and survey findings.
Review quarterly and document corrective actions.
Use survey results to prepare plans of correction and informal dispute resolution.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Screen employees and contractors against Medicare/Medicaid exclusion lists.
STAR+PLUS providers are screened and enrolled with the State (42 CFR 438.602).
Bill the correct STAR+PLUS code (T2031 with level modifier after the ISP renews) and keep supporting documentation.
Staff may report compliance concerns without retaliation.

policies.title: STAR+PLUS Assisted Living Operations (Contracting, Room and Board, Reporting)
state_specifics: Members live in an ALF contracted with their MCO. The contract states the housing option (apartment single/double or non-apartment).
Health assessment and emergency training within 3 days of admission. At least 4 social activities per week.
Report significant changes to the MCO by the next business day. Keep member trust fund records.
Room and board (SSI minus $85 personal needs allowance, $909/month in 2026) cannot be waived (a lower amount may be accepted). It is prorated in month one and due on a written date.
Pay-source rate: HCPCS T2031 with level modifier on the new ISP.

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry, Maintenance, Transportation, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Staffing must be sufficient for cleanliness and laundry (§553.253(c)).
Residents may have visitors at any reasonable hour (§553.267).
Plan for pets and service animals in emergencies (§553.275).
Maintain the building to Subchapter D standards for the license category.

documents.title: Licensing Standards for Assisted Living Facilities, 26 TAC Chapter 553 (Subchapters B, D Div. 2, E, F). Used as the fallback because no single policy-review form exists.
documents.form_number: None. Regulation sections that enumerate required written policies, plans and procedures.
documents.issuer: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), Long-term Care Regulation
documents.version: Current codified chapter. §553.259 and §553.23 were read on the Cornell LII mirror of the TAC (§553.259 shows amendment eff. 12/6/2022). Text for the other sections was read from a third-party reproduction of Chapter 553 (CHA Seminars, 164 pp.), which says it only approximates the rule. Verify against the official TAC. A Dec. 22, 2023 Texas Register proposal would renumber sections, for example §553.275 to §553.295. Confirm current numbering before the manual is finalized.
documents.how_used: Source of every item in required_items. Items keep the rule's own numbering, for example 553.259(c)(4). Only policy, plan, procedure and program content is listed. Application forms, fees, ownership, fire-marshal papers, licenses and physical-plant construction standards are excluded.

documents.title: Assisted Living Facilities Checklist (ALF Health Checklist)
documents.how_used: This is the surveyor's compliance checklist that mirrors Chapter 553, and it is the closest official 'checklist'. Fetching the PDF failed, so it was not itemized. Use it as a cross-check against the items below. The HHSC ALF page also lists PR 2383 (Alzheimer's certification checklist) and the PR 2384-2389 LSC checklists.

documents.title: Initial license application rules (§553.19, §553.23, §553.25(d), §553.29(f))
documents.form_number: Online application through TULIP. No fillable policy checklist found.
documents.issuer: Texas HHSC Licensing and Credentialing, Long-term Care Regulation
documents.how_used: These rules show when policies are reviewed: at the on-site health inspection, or by upload for good-standing applicants. They do not list policy content.

required_items.text: Applicant (good-standing applicant requesting a license before the health inspection) must submit via the online portal: the applicant's policies and procedures; with evidence of compliance with §553.257(b) (Human Resources) and documentation that employees have the credentials in §553.253.

Applicant requesting Alzheimer's certification before the health inspection must submit for approval the applicant's policies and procedures required by Subchapter F, and documentation of compliance with Subchapter F and §553.257(b).

Fire Safety Plan: an ALF must establish a fire safety plan for the protection of all persons in the facility in the event of fire; in effect at all times; written copies available to all supervisory personnel; copy readily available within the facility.

The fire safety plan addresses: (A) evacuation to an area of refuge; (B) evacuation from the building when necessary; (C) special staff actions, including fire protection procedures necessary to ensure the safety of any resident.

Large Type B ALF plan includes the NFPA 101 'Procedure in Case of Fire' provisions (§19.7.2 existing / §18.7.2 new); plan reviewed at least annually and revised; employees instructed on duties at least annually and when revised; plan reflects current evacuation capabilities of residents.

Smoking Policies: an ALF must establish and enforce policies regarding smoking, even if the policy is that smoking will not be permitted. The policy must also address e-cigarettes and vaping devices. If smoking is permitted: designate smoking areas for residents and staff, and provide ashtrays of noncombustible material and safe design.

Fire Alarm System: establish a program to inspect, test, and maintain the fire alarm system per NFPA 72 (and NFPA 720 where CO detection is provided), executed at least every six months through a contract with a State Fire Marshal-registered company; onsite documentation.
Fire Sprinkler System (if equipped): establish a program to inspect, test, and maintain per NFPA 25, executed at least every six months; onsite documentation.

Oxygen: adopt, implement, and enforce procedures for resident use, storage, and handling of oxygen cylinders and liquid oxygen containers in the possession and under the control of residents, to ensure the safety of all residents.

Manager: designate in writing a manager with authority over the operation; manager qualifications, 24-hr management course, 12 hrs annual continuing education, 40 hrs/week on duty; designate in writing an employee competent and authorized to act in the manager's absence.

Staffing: develop and implement staffing policies which require staffing ratios based upon the needs of residents as identified in service plans; disclose the normal 24-hr staffing pattern to prospective residents and post it monthly; sufficient staff for items (A)-(F); night-shift staffing by Type A/Type B and facility size.

Orientation: all staff complete 4 hrs before assuming job responsibilities, covering at minimum: (A) reporting of abuse and neglect; (B) confidentiality of resident information; (C) universal precautions; (D) conditions about which they should notify the facility manager; (E) residents' rights; (F) emergency and evacuation procedures.

Attendants: 16 hrs on-the-job supervision and training within the first 16 hrs following orientation, including (A) assistance with ADLs; (B) residents' health conditions; (C) safety measures to prevent accidents and injuries; (D) emergency first aid procedures; (E) managing disruptive behavior; (F) behavior management; (G) fall prevention.

Direct care staff: 6 hrs annual education, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management (competency-based; addresses unique needs of the facility). Facilities employing licensed nurses, CNAs or certified medication aides: annual in-service training appropriate to job responsibilities (topics A-F).

Alzheimer's training for staff providing personal care to residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders in a non-certified facility: manager 4 hrs plus 2 hrs annual CE; personal care staff 4 hrs plus 2 hrs CE; non-direct-service staff training; competency-based evaluation; training certificates and records.

All Staff Policy: a facility must adopt, implement, and enforce a written policy that (1) requires a facility employee who provides direct care to a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder to successfully complete training in the provision of care to such residents and (2) ensures the care and services provided meet the specific identified needs of the resident relating to the diagnosis.

Training under (a)(1) must include information about: (1) symptoms of dementia; (2) stages of Alzheimer's disease; (3) person-centered behavioral interventions; (4) communication with a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder.

Personnel Records: keep current and complete personnel records including (1) criminal history check; (2) annual Employee Misconduct Registry check; (3) annual Nurse Aide Registry check; (4) initial TB screening; (5) compliance with or exemption from the facility vaccination policy; (6) signed statement acknowledging criminal liability for failure to report abuse, neglect, and exploitation; (7) signed disclosure statement (HSC §250.006 convictions; lived in another state in past five years).

Investigation of Facility Employees: comply with HSC Ch. 250; search EMR and NAR before hire and at least every 12 months, keep results in the personnel file; do not hire or continue to employ persons listed as unemployable or barred by HSC §250.006; give EMR notification per §561.3; name-based criminal history check in prior states of residence (no direct resident contact pending results); suspend employees found by HHSC to have engaged in reportable conduct while appeals are pending.

A facility must not admit or retain a resident whose needs cannot be met by the facility and who cannot secure the necessary services from an outside resource; additional services require written concurrence of the resident, physician, or legal representative.

There must be a written admission agreement between the facility and the resident specifying such details as services to be provided and the charges for the services; statement if services/supplies could be a Medicare benefit.

Share disclosure statement, rate schedule, and service plan with outside resources providing additional services; Memory Care Disclosure Statement (Form 3650) if the facility advertises memory care, and disclose whether Alzheimer's certified (Form 3641 if certified).

Health examination by a physician within 30 days before or 14 days after admission; secure at admission the identifying information in items (A)-(K) (name, SSN, usual residence, sex, marital status, DOB, place of birth, occupation, emergency notification contacts and physician, pharmacy preference, Medicaid/Medicare number).

Resident Assessment and Service Plan: within 14 days of admission, a comprehensive assessment (items A-T, e.g., location admitted from, primary language, sleep-cycle issues, behavioral symptoms, psychosocial issues, dementia history, ADL patterns, cognitive skills, communication, physical functioning, continence, nutrition, oral/dental, diagnoses, medications, special treatments, hospital admissions, preventive health needs) and an individual service plan; service plan signed by resident or responsible person and updated annually and on significant change; respite and emergency admission provisions.

Before admitting, explain and provide the disclosure statement and document receipt; provide the Residents' Bill of Rights; provide the resident's immediate family, and document receipt of, the HHSC abuse/neglect/exploitation hotline number.

The facility must have written policies regarding residents accepted, services provided, charges, refunds, responsibilities of facility and residents, privileges of residents, and other rules and regulations.

Make resident policies available to staff and to residents or responsible parties at admission, with documented notice of changes before the effective date; before or upon admission notify resident/representative of HHSC rules and facility policies on restraint and seclusion; give a written copy of the emergency preparedness plan or an evacuation summary.

Advance Directives: maintain written policies regarding implementation of advance directives, including a clear and precise statement of any procedure the facility is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold; give written notice to residents at admission (order of preference for incapacitated residents).

Inappropriate Placement / evacuation waiver: facility procedures for aging in place and inappropriate placement (Forms 1124, 1125, 1126; detailed emergency plan; evacuation waiver request within 10 working days); disclosure statement must notify resident of the waiver process and the facility's policies and procedures for aging in place; 30-day discharge if not obtained.

Medications: administration per physician's orders by authorized persons (licensed, medication aide, or RN-delegated employee); dispensing through pharmacy; medication profile record contents (name, strength, dosage, amount received, directions, route, Rx number, pharmacy, date issued); supervision limited to listed tasks; monthly counseling for residents who self-administer; immediate reporting of unusual reactions; written record of missed doses.

Storage: locked area for all medications; each resident's medication stored separately; locked refrigerator storage; poisons and 'external use only' medications stored separately; if controlled drugs are stored, facility policies and procedures must address the prevention of the diversion of the controlled drugs.

Disposal: discontinued, deceased-resident and expired medications kept separate and disposed of by a Texas-registered pharmacist; needles and syringes per 25 TAC §§1.131-1.137; release of medications to discharged residents on signed receipt.

Accident, Injury, or Acute Illness: arrange emergency care or transfer; immediately notify physician and next of kin/responsible party/placing agency; describe and document on a separate report with final disposition; stock first aid supplies for burns, cuts, and poisoning in a single location.

Healthcare Professional: coordination of services within scope of practice; facility must not provide ongoing services comparable to a nursing facility; residents may contract with a HCSSA or independent professional.
Activities Program: the facility must provide an activity or social program at least weekly for the residents.

Dietary Services: person designated responsible for food service; at least three meals daily with no more than a 16-hr span between evening meal and breakfast; menus planned one week in advance, followed, variations documented, records kept 30 days; therapeutic diets per physician order (calculated by a dietitian where required); four-day staple and one-day perishable supplies; food sources, storage, temperature, handwashing, sanitation, and employee-illness requirements (items 1-18).

Infection Prevention and Control: each facility must establish, implement, enforce, and maintain an infection prevention and control policy and procedure designed to provide a safe, sanitary, and comfortable environment and help prevent the development and transmission of disease and infection.

Report residents with reportable diseases to the local health authority; written policies for control of communicable disease among employees and residents addressing tuberculosis (TB) screening and a safe and sanitary environment; exclude infected employees from food handling or direct care; employee TB screening within two weeks of employment and annually; resident TB screening consistent with CDC guidelines.

Written policies and procedures for: (A) monitoring key infectious agents, including multidrug-resistant organisms; (B) wearing personal protective equipment and cleaning hands; (C) cleaning and disinfecting environmental surfaces; (D) using universal precautions for blood and bodily fluids; (E) removing soiled items from the environment at least once daily.
Written policy and procedures for making a rapid influenza diagnostic test available to a resident exhibiting flu-like symptoms.

Vaccine-preventable disease policy (HSC Ch. 224): written policy that MUST (i) require employees/contractors providing direct care to receive specified vaccines based on risk; (ii) specify the vaccines; (iii) include verification procedures; (iv) include exemption procedures for CDC contraindications/precautions; (v) include procedures protecting residents from exempt staff; (vi) prohibit discrimination/retaliation against exempt staff; (vii) require records of compliance or exemption; (viii) include disciplinary actions. The policy MAY include conscience exemptions and restrict contact during a public health disaster.

Restraints and Seclusion: all restraints for behavioral management, staff convenience, or discipline are prohibited and seclusion is prohibited; restraint only if physician-authorized in writing (circumstances and duration) or necessary in an emergency; behavioral-emergency definition; prohibited restraint types; acceptable restraint hold; post-restraint physician appointment and 24-hr notification; no retaliation for reporting misuse.

Wheelchair Self-Release Seat Belts: facility must allow use if the four conditions (A)-(D) are met; restraint-free facilities must give residents a written statement; circumstances when the facility need not continue to allow use.

Health Maintenance Activities (only if the facility allows personal care staff to perform HMAs without delegation): RN assessment per 22 TAC §225.6, documented conditions (stable and predictable; resident able to direct; written agreement), and reassessment at least annually (every six months for Alzheimer's residents); otherwise RN delegation under 22 TAC Ch. 225.

Resident Records: treated as confidential and safeguarded from unauthorized use, loss, or destruction; contents (A)-(H); available to residents, legal representatives, and HHSC; simple financial record of charges and of any personal finances entrusted to the facility; receipts upon request.

Guardianship Record Requirements: request the current court order and letters of guardianship at admission, when a guardian is appointed, and at each annual assessment; at least one follow-up request within 30 days; keep documentation and copies in the resident's record.

Residents' Bill of Rights: provide a copy to each resident and post it (in each resident's primary language); each resident's rights (3)(A)-(BB), including freedom from abuse/restraint, complaint rights, mail, visitation, financial management, records confidentiality, physician choice, service-plan participation, refusal of treatment, phone and privacy, personal property, Medicare/Medicaid notice by day 30, transfer/discharge limits and 30-day written notice contents, ombudsman access, advance directive.
Providers' Bill of Rights posted in a prominent place with rights (A)-(J); access to residents for HHSC and local authority employees.

Authorized Electronic Monitoring (AEM): permit AEM; do not refuse admission or discharge because of an AEM request; Form 3100 on admission, Form 0066 request, Form 0067 roommate consent; notice at room entrance; 8.5 x 11 'Electronic Monitoring' notice at main entrance; reasonable physical accommodation; abuse/neglect reporting for recordings.

Ombudsman access: allow the State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility, residents, resident-representative contact information, and records as specified.

Postings: license; HHSC complaint-procedure sign; inspection-report availability notice; most recent inspection report; Residents' Bill of Rights; Providers' Bill of Rights; local and State Ombudsman telephone numbers (800-252-2412); normal 24-hr staffing patterns; abuse/neglect/exploitation hotline sign (800-458-9858).

Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation: staff who have cause to believe a resident has been or may be adversely affected must report to HHSC (800-458-9858 / TxAbuseHotline.org) and local law enforcement; report must include (1)-(5) (resident name, age, address; responsible person; nature and extent of condition; basis of knowledge; other relevant information).
An ALF must follow its internal policies regarding the prevention, detection, and reporting of abuse, neglect, or exploitation.

Immediately make an oral report to HHSC, investigate the allegation, and send a written report of the investigation to HHSC state office no later than the fifth calendar day after the oral report; no retaliation for good-faith complaints; require staff, as a condition of employment, to sign a statement of possible criminal liability for failure to report.

Risk assessment: conduct and document a risk assessment for internal and external emergencies or disasters relevant to the facility's operations and location (e.g., fire/explosion; power, telecommunication or water outage; wildfire; hazardous materials; active shooter/bomb threat; flood; hurricane/severe weather; epidemic/pandemic; cyber-attack; loss of all or part of the facility).

Written emergency preparedness and response plan based on the risk assessment, addressing the eight core functions: Direction and Control; Warning; Communication; Sheltering Arrangements; Evacuation; Transportation; Health and Medical Needs; Resource Management. The plan must document EMC contact information, include a process for communication with the EMC, and the location of a current resident list identifying residents with Alzheimer's/related disorders, evacuation waivers, and mobility or special needs; notify the EMC of the plan.

Plan maintenance: current printed copy in a central location accessible to staff, residents and representatives; review at least annually and after events, with updates within 30 days of shortcomings, drills, or policy/rule changes; document reviews; written copy or evacuation summary to residents/representatives; notify residents how to register with 2-1-1 Texas; register as a provider with 2-1-1 Texas.

Core Function One, Direction and Control: designate the Emergency Preparedness Coordinator (EPC) and an alternate EPC; assign responsibilities to staff by function or position and describe how each staff member understands their role.

Core Function Two, Warning: procedures for notifying the EPC of a disaster; who the EPC will notify (including off hours, weekends, holidays); procedure for keeping persons in the facility informed; procedures for monitoring local news and weather.

Core Function Three, Communication: primary and alternate modes of communication; when to call 911; location of contact lists (representatives and emergency contacts, receiving facilities with written acknowledgements, HCSSA/professionals, staff, resident population); public status communication; procedure for notifying staff, residents, representatives, emergency contacts, HCSSAs, receiving facilities, drivers, and the EMC.

Core Function Four, Sheltering Arrangements: procedure for deciding to remain in the facility (access to medication, records, equipment, water and food including special diets; safe power and temperatures between 68 and 82 degrees F; sheltering staff); notify the HHSC regional office and EMC after deciding to remain.

Core Function Five, Evacuation: evacuation destinations and routes with a map; decision procedure with contingencies and a plan for pets/service animals; documented acknowledgment from at least one receiving facility/destination and one alternate; procedures and responsible staff (D)(i)-(x) for notification of HHSC and EMC, staff accompaniment, resident accounting and tracking, release of resident information, re-entry determination, return of residents.

Core Function Six, Transportation: arrangements for sufficient vehicles; staff designated to drive and communication methods; procedures for safely transporting residents, staff and others; safe transport of and timely access to oxygen, medications, records, food, water, equipment, and supplies.

Core Function Seven, Health and Medical Needs: identify special services residents use (dialysis, oxygen, hospice); procedures to enable continued services; procedures to notify HCSSAs and independent professionals of an evacuation.

Core Function Eight, Resource Management: plan for obtaining, transporting and storing medications, records, food, water, equipment and supplies; staff assigned by position/function; procedure to keep medications secure and at proper temperature; safeguards for confidentiality, security, and integrity of resident records.

Receiving Facility (only if the facility will act as one): plan must include procedures for accommodating temporary emergency placement from another ALF, subject to conditions (1)-(5) (capacity limits, safety, ability to meet needs, log, continuity-of-care items).

Plan training: annual staff training; train staff on responsibilities before assuming duties and when responsibilities change; at least one unannounced annual drill; offer and document training to residents, representatives and emergency contacts; document compliance.

Self-reported incidents: report fires (call 800-458-9858; Form 3707 within 15 days); report death, serious injury or threat from a disaster (call immediately; Provider Investigation Report Form 3613-A within five working days). Emergency Response System: administrator and designee enroll and respond in the format established by HHSC.
Certified Alzheimer's facility: manager/unit supervisor qualifications (age 21 and education/experience options) and six hours annual continuing education on dementia care.

Alzheimer's staff training: 4 hrs dementia-specific orientation (causes/progression/management; managing dysfunctional behavior; safety risks); attendants 16 hrs on-the-job training (ADLs; emergency and evacuation procedures specific to dementia population; managing dysfunctional behavior; behavior management); attendants 12 hrs annual in-service on Alzheimer's.

Staffing: employ sufficient staff to meet the needs of Alzheimer's residents; in large facilities or units with 17 or more residents, two staff members immediately available when residents are present.

Admission procedures, assessment and service plan: use Form 3641; establish pre-admission procedures (application process, interviews, home visits) to ensure appropriate placement; give Form 3641 to any inquirer; comprehensive assessment within 14 days and annually; individualized service plan within 14 days, updated annually and on significant change.

Activities program: planned and structured program with a balanced mixture of cognitive, recreational and ADL activities; individualized; daily offerings and minimum structured hours; employee responsible for activities (activity director for 20 hrs weekly in facilities of 17 or more residents); monthly schedule; six hours annual continuing education; special equipment as appropriate.

official.notes: Texas HHSC publishes no single policy-review form for ALF initial licensing. <cite index="24-2">HHSC's ALF page lists an ALF Health Checklist (PR 2382) among its resources.</cite> <cite index="23-4">The checklist items represent 26 TAC Chapter 553.</cite> I could not fetch that PDF, so the items above come from the Chapter 553 sections that require written policies, plans or procedures. How policies are reviewed: an applicant files through the TULIP online portal, and HHSC then conducts an LSC inspection. After the facility has admitted one to three residents, the applicant notifies HHSC that it is ready for the on-site health inspection, which tests compliance with the Subchapter E operating and resident-care standards (§553.23(f)). The manual is reviewed against those standards at that inspection. A good-standing applicant (six years of Type A/B operation, no harm or sanction history) can instead request a license before the health inspection. That applicant must upload the policies and procedures plus evidence of §553.257(b) compliance and staff credentials (§553.25(d)). <cite index="7-3">A good-standing Alzheimer's-certification applicant must submit its Subchapter F policies via the online portal.</cite> Suggested organization: one manual tab per section in the order of 'sections' above, with the Rule cite at the top of each policy so a surveyor can trace it. Include the HHSC forms the rules require (3647 disclosure statement, 3650 and 3641 memory-care and Alzheimer's disclosure statements, 3100/0066/0067 for electronic monitoring, 3707 fire report, 3613-A investigation report, 4719 fire drill report). Use the current HHSC versions of these forms. Caveats: (1) Text for sections other than §553.19, §553.23 and §553.259 was read from a third-party reproduction that says it approximates the rule. Verify wording and numbering against the official TAC. (2) A Dec. 2023 Texas Register proposal would renumber sections (for example §553.275 to §553.295), so confirm the in-force numbering. (3) Items marked conditional (§553.263 HMA, §553.275(m) receiving facility, Subchapter F, §553.104(h) sprinklers) apply only if the facility does those things. (4) Excluded from the list: physical-plant construction standards, license fees, ownership and controlling-person disclosures, fire-authority documentation (§553.19(c)), and pre-licensure training certificates.
